items.title: Ran Blake interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 16, 2021
items.q: Abbey and Max doing — I should mention last names, Roach and Lincoln — doing “Freedom Day.” ... Max Roach’s piece

ctx.x: Oh that’s very interesting. Some of these thoughts that I have and these questions, I don’t really honestly think they have an answer. Like what does music mean? What can it mean if it’s an abstract art form, especially if there’s no singing? There’s no clear story. So will it affect different people very differently.

I know that I try to have a written program. First it’s sort of a nuisance to people to get them to type it up, and secondly some people arriving at a club just a minute before don’t read the program notes. Once in a while I have the courage to get up and speak or often I have somebody that will represent me. I don’t like to speak much because then I go out of my mood of playing and trying to deal with the audience and when lights go on I get back to the present life. But you’re very, very right, like somebody…

Abbey and Max doing — I should mention last names, Roach and Lincoln — doing “Freedom Day.” And somebody just hearing it instrumentally without the words might think it’s, or they may have heard one word, freedom, they may think freedom to get out of school in May. I want summer. I don’t want discipline. So rarely do they get it right. But this might hold the music together for me and other people. I know when my “Blue Potato” came out, my third or fourth record, at the same time Charles Haden’s “Liberation…
